subject: general
question: Which ruler succeeded Chandragupta Maurya in 297 BCE?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara** was the second ruler of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• He succeeded his father, **Chandragupta Maurya**, in **297 BCE**.
 
• Bindusara was known by the title **Amitraghata**, which means "**Slayer of Enemies**".
 
• His reign was marked by the consolidation of the Mauryan empire, which was already expanded under Chandragupta.
 
• Bindusara maintained friendly relations with the **Hellenistic kingdoms** and received ambassadors like **Dionysius** from Egypt.
 
• He ruled for approximately **25 years** and was succeeded by his son, **Ashoka the Great**.
 
• Bindusara expanded the empire further into the **Deccan region**, excluding areas like Kalinga.
 
• Historical texts like the **Mahavamsa** and writings of **Greek historians** provide insights into his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kumaragupta**__

 __
 
• **Kumaragupta** was a ruler of the **Gupta Empire**, not the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He ruled in the 5th century CE and is known for founding the **Nalanda University**.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Gupta Empire's prosperity and cultural achievements.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 __
 
• **Ashoka**, also known as **Ashoka the Great**, was the son of Bindusara and succeeded him as the Mauryan ruler.
 
• He is renowned for his role in spreading **Buddhism** across Asia after the **Kalinga War**.
 
• Ashoka's reign marked one of the most celebrated eras in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Kanishka**__
 
 
• **Kanishka** was a ruler of the **Kushan Empire**, not related to the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• He is famous for his contributions to **Buddhism** and initiating the **Kanishka Era** in 78 CE.
 
• Kanishka's reign witnessed the spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and China.
